title: Perf observability sync snapshot 2025-06-18
content:
Summary:

Quick sync from today's performance/observability working group (2025-06-18). Focus: recent p99 latency bump in us-west-2, verifying whether kernel selection changes or KV cache behavior is the primary cause, and sanity-checking throughput after the autoscaler tweak.

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (owner)
- Tomás Chen (profiling lead)
- Nina Morgan (SRE oncall)
- Ravi Kapoor (runtime infra)
- Lena Ortiz (product/console)
- Brief drop-in: Jorge (bench infra)

Meeting goals:
1) Triage short-term customer impact and set mitigation path.
2) Run focused reproductions and agree on next experiments.
3) Assign owners and deadlines for follow-ups.

Observed problem statement:
- Starting ~2025-06-14, we saw a ~9–15% increase in p99 generation latency for long-context chat workloads (avg seq_len 1.2k, KV hit rate estimated ~68%) on us-west-2 dedicated clusters. Individual slots show higher variance (p95 unaffected).
- Throughput (tokens/sec) nominal across most traffic, but a subset of requests saw token emission stalls (20–40ms micro-pauses every ~200 tokens).
- No deploys on serving-runtime code on 6/14–6/17, but there was an ops change: kernel selection table update rolled 6/13 (PR #842) to prefer fused-attn on A100-80GB where available.

Quick metrics snapshot (from console - sampling window 06/16–06/18):
- p50: 44ms -> steady
- p95: 152ms -> steady
- p99: 412ms -> 460ms (12% increase)
- avg tokens/sec (batch-level): 1850 -> 1820 (1.6% drop)
- KV cache local hit rate: 0.68 -> 0.65 (estimated)
- Error rate: unchanged

Reproduction attempts (what we ran during meeting):
1) Local isolated reproducer (Tomás): run-id run-2025-06-18-A. Config: model: rw-k-v1-qa (19B), seq_len=1200, batch=8, temp=0.0, kv-cache enabled. Observed micro-pauses with fused-attn kernel, but when forcing unfused kernel, pausing disappeared but end-to-end latency increased slightly for small sequences.
Command snippet used:
- bench-run --model rw-k-v1-qa --seq 1200 --batch 8 --kv-cache --k-config fused --runs 50 --report micro-pauses
Result: 48/50 runs showed periodic 25–40ms stalls, median stall interval ~215 tokens.

2) Canary on dedicated pool (Ravi): incrementally rolled back kernel-table on a small subset (10 nodes). Canary id cny-2025-06-18-01. Traffic routed 2% -> observed p99 drop back to baseline for canary.

3) KV cache stress test (Jorge): evict-heavy workload to validate caching thresholds. When cache fill drops <60% we see similar stall signature (but larger magnitude). Eviction pattern correlated with multi-tenant noisy neighbors.

Hypotheses discussed:
- H1 (kernel selection regression): kernel change causes periodic context flush/rehash inside fused-attn path, creating brief stalls under particular token alignment conditions. Evidence: canary rollback helps, local forcing of unfused kernel removes stalls.
- H2 (KV cache eviction/rehab): eviction pressure from co-located tasks exposes a path in the runtime where loaded KV pages are rehydrated synchronously, causing short stalls. Evidence: eviction stress reproduces similar pause pattern.
- H3 (scheduler/backpressure interaction): autoscaler/queueing change earlier this week slightly altered queuing shape -> triggers larger contiguous batches at certain windows causing microburst behavior. Evidence: small change in batch distribution observed but weaker.

Decisions and next experiments (agreed):
1) Short-term mitigation: revert kernel-table change for all affected hosts (Ops). Owner: Ravi. Target: revert to previous kernel table for us-west-2 dedicated pool by 2025-06-19 15:00 PST. Rollback plan documented in PR #842.
2) Add a guards-in-runtime quick patch to make KV rehydration async-friendly (best-effort) for non-critical request paths. Owner: Tomás. Target: 2025-06-22. Patch will add metrics and a kill-switch flag.
3) Isolated repro matrix: Tomás + Jorge to run 3x matrix across seq_len {512,1024,1200}, batch {4,8,12}, kv_hit_rate {0.5,0.65,0.8}, kernel {fused,unfused}. Deliverable: spreadsheet of stall frequency and mean stall ms by 2025-06-20.
4) Autoscaler telemetry: Nina to fetch queue-length histograms across last 30d and compare pre/post 6/13. Action by 2025-06-19 EOD.
5) Customer comms: Lena to prepare templated note for affected customers (mid-enterprise) outlining we are investigating latency micro-pauses and will provide ETA. Draft by 2025-06-19 12:00.

Notes from quick code inspection (Tomás):
- fused-attn path has an index mapping table for token-block alignment. There's a conditional that will re-evaluate mapping when a block boundary is crossed; under certain alignment sequences this triggers synchronous GPU kernel rebind and a barrier.
- The previous kernel-table used a slightly different fallback order that avoided that mapping lookup in common token alignment; PR #842 changed ordering for perf reasons but didn't exercise these alignment cases in CI panel.

Risk assessment:
- Reverting kernel-table might cost a small steady-state perf decrease on p50 for small sequences (~2–3% median), but reduces p99 spikes which are customer-facing. Ops approved short-term revert.
- Async KV rehydrate patch is low-risk but needs load test for regressions in memory / GC behavior.

Action items (one-line list):
- Ravi: revert kernel-table in us-west-2 dedicated pool (target 2025-06-19 15:00 PST).
- Tomás: implement asynchronous rehydrate flag + metrics (target 2025-06-22).
- Jorge: run eviction and repro matrix runs, upload CSV to bench-gcs and slack post (target 2025-06-20).
- Nina: provide autoscaler / queue histograms and correlation with request size (target 2025-06-19 EOD).
- Lena: customer comms draft (target 2025-06-19 12:00).

Open questions / parking lot:
- Do we need a new unit/integration test that exercises token-block alignment cases? (likely yes)
- Should kernel-table updates require a small alignment run in CI with long-seq jobs? (proposal: add 1 long-seq nightly)
- How often do we rotate the kernel-table? Could we avoid global pushes and instead use staged per-hardware profiles?

Notes-to-self (choppy):
- remember to add metric: stall-count-per-1e6-tokens -> will help track micro-pauses
- capture full perf traces for a run with and without fused kernel: use perf-trace-collector v2 (cmd in bench-readme)
- double-check memory pinning on A100 80GB nodes after rollback

Related artifacts referenced during meeting:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842 (kernel selection change)
- JIRA: INF-2987 (customer report / incident)
- Bench infra: gs://bench-results/2025/06/kv-evict-run-06-18.csv

Next sync:
- Follow-up quick sync Thursday 2025-06-19 16:00 PST to verify canary/revert results.

End of notes.

(Informal tone, contains raw reproducer commands, TODOs and tentative timelines — save as working doc)
